In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of neutrino properties and the search for new physics in the neutrino sector.
a novel mechanism for the generation of late time neutrino masses, and the possible experimental consequences of such a scenario.
the possibility that neutrinos from relic supernovae may provide a unique probe of the physics of the early universe and of neutrino mass models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current and future observations of SN neutrinos will either provide a direct proof for low scale models, or provide an upper limit on the neutrino mass, which is much stronger than any other limit.

the MiniZebra experiment, in combination with future neutrino experiments, will allow to probe neutrino masses down to 0.1eV, and will be able to detect relic supernova neutrino bursts at distances as far as 1Mpc.

the current and future neutrino experiments may be able to provide us with a direct evidence of the low scale of symmetry breakdown, and hence a possible window into the physics of the early Universe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, the observation of neutrino burst from a nearby SN, with a flux suppressed by at least a factor of 100, would provide the first direct evidence for the existence of a light scalar with mass of order MeV.
, in the context of the low scale models, the diffuse SRN are a unique tool for the study of neutrino properties.
a new window for neutrino mass measurement is opened.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the study of the diffuse SRN flux can provide a direct probe of neutrino properties.

a low scale of new physics, such as that of the seesaw mechanism for neutrino mass generation, can have dramatic observable consequences for the SN neutrino burst, which can be tested by future experiments.

the observation of a significant suppression of the neutrino flux from nearby SN bursts, or the observation of a large number of neutrinos from a nearby SN burst, would be a spectacular direct evidence of light bosons and would be the first direct evidence for neutrinos being massive.
